## Findings

### 1. BLOCKER - the rapid law and the holder law miss material between the probe points

`crates/simview/src/check/stock.rs:46-59` (`disc_in_material`), used at `stock.rs:101` (rapid) and `stock.rs:105` (shank and holder bands).

The probe reads the disc at only nine points: the centre and eight points on a circle of radius `r - cell`. Across the path, the probes are at the lateral offsets 0, ±0.71(r - cell) and ±(r - cell). Material that stands only between these offsets is not seen. The check then prints PASS.

Reproduction (fanuc dialect, stock `0,0,-10,40,40,0`, `T1=10`, `--cell 0.25`):

```
G0 X-10. Y14. Z10.
G0 Z-5.
G1 X50. F600.       (cuts Y9..Y19 to Z-5)
G0 Z10.
G0 X-10. Y26.
G0 Z-5.
G1 X50. F600.       (cuts Y21..Y31 to Z-5; a wall Y19..Y21 stays, top Z0)
G0 Z10.
G0 X-10. Y18.5
G0 Z-3.
G0 X50.             (line 18: the 10 mm tool covers Y13.5..Y23.5 at Z-3)
```

Result: `PASS        stock: 12 moves cut, 10 rapids clear of material`. The rapid at line 18 drives the tool 3 mm deep through the 2 mm wall over its full 40 mm length. The same program with the rapid at `Y20.` gives `FAIL stock: line 18: the rapid runs T1 through material`. So the wall is in the stock, and only the probe pattern misses it.

The holder band uses the same nine points on a larger radius. For a 40 mm holder, the rim points are about 13 mm apart, so a narrow rib under the holder can pass in the same way.

Fix request:
- Sample the full disc (rings and points no more than one cell apart), or use a minimum-distance read over the swept disc.
- Add a pin with a rib between the probe offsets (the program above is sufficient). It must be red on this head.

### 2. Nit (non-blocking) - `crates/simview/src/check/mod.rs:497` and `:517`

`before` is always false at this call, because no check fails before `post_checks`. Thus `|| before` has no effect. If a check moves before `post_checks` later, a post failure can also print a PASS line for the post. Use `if r.failed() == before` (no new failure), or remove `before`.
